Definitions

Glossary

Terms used on this site.

ArduPilot
Open-source autopilot software used on real drones. It runs the fast inner control loop (100-400 Hz).
Audit log
audit.jsonl: one line per Shield decision that found a violation, so every repair can be checked later.
Brake
The Shield's stop command: every velocity value (vx, vy, vz and yaw rate) set to zero. The first step of the escalation state machine.
Bundle
The deployable package of a policy: the IR plus a hash, a version number and a signature, so a flight can prove which rules it used.
CSP
Constraint Summary Pack: a short summary of the active rules that the Prefix Compiler places in front of the VLA prompt.
Escalation state machine
The Shield's fail-safe ladder in the grant's design: Normal → Brake → Loiter (hold position) → RTL (return to launch) → Land, stepping up when violations repeat or a repair would be too large.
Fail-safe trigger correctness
Acceptance KPI: the fail-safe triggers when it is expected to, and not when it is not. The grant's target is at least 99 %.
FenceGuard
Part of our hand-written pilot that reads the policy and slows or steers around zones before the Shield has to act. Our addition, not in the grant.
GeoFence
ArduPilot's own fence (FENCE_ENABLE, FENCE_TYPE, FENCE_ACTION), the last backstop behind the Shield in the grant's design.
Guardrail
Our name for the whole safety layer between the pilot and the autopilot: policy, Prefix Compiler, Shield and logs.
HUD
Head-up display: text and panels drawn over the video, here showing the rules and their status.
IR
Intermediate Representation: the parsed, checked, in-memory form of the policy that the Prefix Compiler and the Shield read.
Jetson Orin
NVIDIA's embedded computer for robots and drones. In the grant's hil and flight topologies it runs the VLA and the Shield.
KPI
Key Performance Indicator: a number the contract uses to accept the work. The grant lists five acceptance KPIs.
MAVLink
The message protocol ArduPilot uses with ground stations and companion computers.
MAVROS 2
The ROS 2 package that translates ROS 2 topics into MAVLink, the message protocol ArduPilot understands.
Mean repair magnitude
KPI: on average, how much the Shield changed a command (in m/s here).
Mean time to safe
Acceptance KPI: the average time from a violation until the drone is back in a safe state.
Mission Planner
ArduPilot's ground-station software: map, parameters and flight monitoring over MAVLink.
Mission success rate
KPI: share of missions that reach their goal with no P0 violation.
NFZ
No-fly zone: a polygon the drone must not enter (polygon_fence in the policy).
Obstacle clearance
Minimum distance from mapped obstacles such as buildings, trees and lamp arms; 3 m in the CityLife policy.
OpenVLA / AerialVLA
OpenVLA is an open-source VLA model; AerialVLA is a drone version of it. Both have flown through the Shield in simulation.
OWL-ViT
Google's open-vocabulary object detector: text in, boxes out. Our city demos use it, instead of a VLA, to find the target.
P0 / P1 / P2
Rule priority. P0 is the most important (safety), e.g. the NFZ; P1 covers limits such as speed; P2 is the lowest.
P0 violation escape rate
Acceptance KPI, target 0. Measured here as the share of ticks on which a P0 violation is still present in the command actually sent to the drone.
Paraphraser
Rewrites a task instruction or a rule summary in different words, so that a test can check whether the mission result stays the same.
Perception rail
The camera-based simulation path: camera images → VLA → Shield → MAVROS 2 → ArduPilot as one system.
Policy DSL
The rule language: flight rules (no-fly zones, altitude and speed limits, corridors, time windows) written in a YAML or JSON file, called a policy.
policy_hash
A fingerprint of the policy content. If one rule changes, the hash changes, so logs and KPI numbers can be matched to the exact rules.
Prefix Compiler
WP2. Builds the CSP from the policy and the mission so the VLA knows the rules before it decides.
Project AirSim
A photo-realistic drone simulator on Unreal Engine 5. Our city demonstrations run here, flown by Project AirSim's own flight controller.
Repair operator
A small function in the Shield that changes a command just enough to obey one kind of rule, e.g. SpeedClamp or GeofenceSlide.
ROS 2
Robot Operating System 2: middleware in which programs (nodes) exchange messages on named topics.
Safety Shield
WP3. Software between the pilot and the autopilot that checks every command, repairs it, or stops the drone.
SITL
Software-In-The-Loop: the real ArduPilot code running as a program on a PC, with simulated sensors.
Stand-off
Minimum distance from the tracked target, e.g. 5 m from a car or 10 m from a person (subject_standoff).
Stress testing
WP4: many scenarios in which rules change mid-flight, run automatically to compute the KPIs.
Tick
One round of the control loop: 0.1 s at 10 Hz.
Topology (dev / hil / flight)
Where the software runs. dev: everything on one desktop. hil: simulators on the desktop, VLA and Shield on a Jetson Orin. flight: the Orin on a real drone.
VLA
Vision-Language-Action model: an AI model that looks at a camera image, reads an instruction, and outputs a movement command.
